stories.title: Tornado causes damage in Detroit’s eastside
stories.summary: A tornado with 115 mph winds struck Detroit’s eastside, causing significant damage and a power outage that delayed a utility regulator meeting. Climate change is linked to increased storm risks.

stories.title: Total Investment in Facility Master Plan Projects Reaches $99.95M
stories.summary: The Facility Master Plan dashboard reports a total investment of $99.95 million across 11 projects. As of October 2025, 7 projects are in Pre-Planning, 1 in Planning, and 2 already completed.

stories.summary: Trans-Siberian Orchestra has announced its 30th Anniversary Winter Tour, set to take place at Little Caesars Arena on December 23, 2026. The event marks a significant milestone for the band's long-running holiday tour tradition.

stories.title: Tribal leaders, clean water advocates rally in Lansing as Line 5 fight intensifies
stories.summary: Tribal leaders and environmental advocates gathered in Lansing to oppose Enbridge's Line 5 pipeline, emphasizing concerns about potential oil spills in the Great Lakes and the proposed tunnel project's impact on sacred sites. The rally, organized by the Anishinaabe Friendship Center, featured calls for decommissioning the pipeline and highlighted the spiritual and environmental significance of the Straits of Mackinac.

photo.alt: Rally against Enbridge's Line 5 pipeline at the Michigan State Capitol.

stories.title: Trinity Health in Livonia to lay off 557 employees starting in October, primarily in IT support
stories.summary: Trinity Health, headquartered in Livonia, will permanently lay off 557 employees primarily in IT support starting October 25 and continuing through November 29. The layoffs follow a decision to outsource technology services, but a law firm is investigating potential violations of the WARN Act due to a 60-day notice period discrepancy.

stories.title: Tripadvisor Travelers’ Choice Award 2024 for top 10% worldwide attractions
stories.summary: The museum won Tripadvisor’s 'Travelers’ Choice Award 2024', placing it in the top 10% of worldwide attractions based on millions of reviews.

stories.title: Trump Administration Rolls Back Power Plant Emission Rules
stories.summary: The Trump administration announced it will roll back rules governing power plant emissions, despite scientific consensus on climate change. Rachel Rothschild, an assistant professor at Michigan Law, discusses the implications of this decision.

photo.alt: Stateside podcast cover image

stories.title: Trump likes data centers. Congress seems stuck. The midterms could deliver a verdict.
stories.summary: Political battles over data centers are intensifying in close House and Senate races, with candidates clashing over local control and federal regulation. Sen. Jon Husted's ratepayer protection bill was blocked in the Senate, while House lawmakers left Washington without addressing key issues before the Nov. 8 election. The outcome of these races may determine whether Congress acts on data center policies or leaves decisions to local communities.

photo.alt: Trump likes data centers. Congress seems stuck. The midterms could deliver a verdict.

stories.title: Trump pushes daylight saving; clocks expected to change
stories.summary: Daylight saving time ends at 2 a.m. local time on Sunday, Nov. 1, when clocks move back one hour to 1 a.m. The shift marks the return to standard time and gives Americans an extra hour of sleep, while also bringing earlier sunsets and more morning daylight through the winter months.

photo.alt: Trump pushes daylight saving; clocks expected to change

stories.title: Trump's clock plan could affect Halloween
stories.summary: President Donald Trump's proposal to make daylight saving time permanent could impact Halloween, potentially requiring trick-or-treaters to end activities earlier. While the House passed legislation for year-round daylight saving time, the Senate's recess until Sept. 14 and uncertainty about sufficient votes leave the issue unresolved before the Nov. 1 clock change.

photo.alt: Portrait of Saman Shafiq

stories.title: U-M’s proposed computing center draws concerns over role in nuclear weapons modernization
stories.summary: Explores concerns about the University of Michigan and Los Alamos National Laboratory’s proposed computing facility in Ypsilanti Township, which would conduct classified nuclear weapons modernization research.

photo.alt: Michigan Data Center Report

stories.title: U.S. Supreme Court ruled against Trump . . . for now
stories.summary: The U.S. Supreme Court rejected President Donald Trump's mail-in ballots executive order. However, Conservative Justice Brett Kavanaugh left open the possibility of future implementation. Twenty-one states, including Michigan, and the District of Columbia filed a lawsuit blocking the USPS plan, leading to a preliminary injunction.

stories.title: U.S. Supreme Court ruled against Trump . . . for now
stories.summary: The U.S. Supreme Court upheld a preliminary injunction blocking the USPS from implementing new mail-in ballot requirements from an executive order. This decision preserves the current election process for the upcoming November election but leaves open the possibility of future changes. A new poll shows declining voter confidence in Michigan's election system, with 74.4% of likely voters believing it is fair and accurate, down from 79.4% in 2025.

source.name: Kalloli Bhatt, Zoe Clark, Rick Pluta

stories.title: Uber driver killed, passenger ejected in Oak Park crash
stories.summary: An Uber driver was killed and a passenger ejected in a crash in Oak Park. Later, a second driver with a blood alcohol level three times the legal limit struck an unoccupied patrol car during the traffic diversion. The driver was arrested for operating under the influence, and bodycam footage was shared to raise awareness about drunk driving dangers.

photo.alt: Uber driver killed, passenger ejected in Oak Park crash

stories.title: UM Detroit Center’s Block x Block series: Open dialogue on issues of concern, centering Detroiters’ lived experiences
stories.summary: The University of Michigan Detroit Center (UMDC) launches the Block x Block series, a monthly public engagement initiative featuring two speakers per event - a community leader and a UM faculty member - to discuss systemic issues like immigration, LGBTQ+ rights, and housing through open dialogue. The program emphasizes Detroiters' lived experiences and aims to foster university-community collaborations by prioritizing face-to-face conversations over traditional panels.

photo.alt: Block x Block Monthly Lecture Flyer

stories.title: Unless a buyer steps up, the Toledo Blade to print last edition at the end of the year
stories.summary: The Toledo Blade, a nearly 200-year-old newspaper in Northwest Ohio, will print its final edition by year's end unless a buyer emerges. Current owners Block Communications made the decision due to unsustainable financial losses, following a rejected contract proposal by the NewsGuild that would have cut benefits and allowed AI to replace journalists. The paper previously avoided closure when a nonprofit bought The Pittsburgh Post-Gazette under similar circumstances.

source.name: Beenish Ahmed, The Associated Press, Stateside Staff

photo.alt: A delivery van for the Toledo Blade, a nearly 200-year-old paper in Northwest Ohio, is parked in a lot.

stories.title: Urbanism Club takes over downtown parking spots for ‘Park(ing) Day’
stories.summary: University of Michigan students and Ann Arbor residents transformed three State Street parking spots into community spaces for games and reflection during ‘Park(ing) Day’. The annual event, held on Sept. 18, aims to highlight the potential of repurposing urban parking spaces for public use. Organized by the U-M Urbanism Club and local groups, the event featured chalk art, seating areas, and discussions on reimagining city spaces.

photo.alt: People using parking spots as community spaces with tables and chairs.

stories.title: Urbanism Club takes over downtown parking spots for ‘Park(ing) Day’
stories.summary: University of Michigan students and Ann Arbor residents transformed three State Street parking spots into community spaces for Park(ing) Day, featuring tables, chairs, and activities. The event, organized by the Urbanism Club and Neighbors for More Neighbors, aimed to demonstrate how urban land could be repurposed for public use rather than parking. Participants reflected on community connections while advocating for reduced car-centric city planning.

photo.alt: People gather on the sidewalk.

stories.title: Van Zile Vacant Building Demolition Begins in Summer 2023
stories.summary: The Van Zile project involves demolishing a vacant building, starting in Summer 2023 and expected to complete by Fall 2029. The project is currently in the Pre-Planning stage with no specified investment amount.

stories.title: Veterans targeted by postcard scams offering fake benefits
stories.summary: Scammers are using postcards to target veterans with counterfeit benefits, including fake dental coverage and a non-existent savings program. Additional scams deliver unexpected items to veterans' homes, with QR codes that may lead to malware or phishing sites. Veterans are advised to contact the VA hotline and report scams to official channels.

photo.alt: Veterans targeted by postcard scams offering fake benefits

stories.title: Wade McCree Advancement of Justice Award
stories.summary: Lauren Gibbons earned the 2024 Wade H. McCree Advancement of Justice Award for her investigation into how court fees in Michigan's juvenile justice system burden families with crippling debt, leading to legislative reforms.

stories.title: Washtenaw Business Lens: How AI is transforming the way people do business
stories.summary: Jonah Bailey and Andy LaBarre discuss AI's impact on industries like manufacturing, healthcare, and software, emphasizing the need for guardrails, ethical considerations, and the urgency for businesses to adapt. They highlight challenges in customer behavior prediction, data center sustainability, and AI-generated content transparency.

stories.title: Washtenaw County weighs landfill expansion, Northville residents object
stories.summary: Northville Township residents oppose GFL’s proposed Arbor Hills Landfill expansion in Salem Township due to past pollution and unapproved height increases. Washtenaw County is weighing waste reduction against landfill space needs, with further discussion scheduled for Nov. 18.

stories.title: Washtenaw United: SafeHouse Center continues to serve those recovering from domestic violence with help from the community
stories.summary: SafeHouse Center's Executive Director Christine Watson discusses the organization's role in supporting domestic violence survivors, challenges with affordable housing, and the importance of community partnerships. Watson emphasizes the need for continued investment in resources to ensure survivors can transition safely from temporary shelter to stable housing and community integration.

stories.title: Wayne County transit millage faces lawsuit ahead of August ballot
stories.summary: SMART and Wayne County officials state they have not been served with the lawsuit and will defend against allegations once served. stories.summary: WCC has received multiple honors and awards from state and local leaders, including the Environmental Excellence Partnership Program Award, Distinguished Service Award, and a tribute from Governor Gretchen Whitmer. stories.summary: The Muslim Student Association at WCC hosted a Ramadan Annual Iftar event to bring students together through faith and education. stories.summary: Historic Blum Barn, a wedding venue in Bridgewater Township, continues hosting weddings after a January fire destroyed its main barn. stories.title: Week of events celebrating Ann Arbor tech to return in September
stories.summary: Registration is now open for Ann Arbor SPARK’s a2Tech360, an annual weeklong series of events spotlighting Ann Arbor’s tech sector, which will return Sept. 22-Oct. 2. The event is organized by Ann Arbor SPARK and aims to highlight the region’s technology innovations and industry growth.

photo.alt: Ann Arbor SPARK board chair Kelly Sexton speaks at SPARK's annual meeting.

stories.title: What could winter be like in Michigan? Early predictions from Almanac
stories.summary: The Old Farmer's Almanac explains how the polar vortex and Quasi-Biennial Oscillation (QBO) influence winter forecasts for Michigan. Weakening of the polar vortex can bring colder Arctic air southward, leading to extreme winter weather outbreaks in the region.

photo.alt: What could winter be like in Michigan? Early predictions from Almanac

stories.title: What will fall be like in Michigan? AccuWeather, NWS say warm and dry
stories.summary: Michigan's fall weather forecast for 2026 predicts warm and dry conditions, influenced by a potent El Niño event. NOAA's Michelle L'Heureux notes the El Niño duration is typical, with no atypical starting season or potential length. The forecast aligns with reports from AccuWeather and the National Weather Service.

photo.alt: What will fall be like in Michigan? AccuWeather, NWS say warm and dry

stories.title: When does daylight saving time end in 2026?
stories.summary: Unless Congress acts, daylight saving time is scheduled to end at 2 a.m. local time on Sunday, Nov. 1, 2026, when clocks move back one hour to 1 a.m. The shift provides an extra hour of sleep but results in earlier sunsets during winter. The change is unlikely to affect Halloween, as it occurs after the holiday on Oct. 31.

photo.alt: Daylight saving time clock change illustration

stories.title: When will Daylight Saving Time end in 2026?
stories.summary: Daylight Saving Time will end at 2 a.m. on Nov. 1, 2026, with clocks set back one hour. President Trump has urged senators to pass the Sunshine Protection Act, which would make DST permanent, but the bill's Senate approval remains uncertain.

photo.alt: When will Daylight Saving Time end in 2026?

stories.title: When will DST begin in 2027?
stories.summary: We'll spring forward at 2 a.m. on March 14, 2027, with clocks to be set one hour forward, marking the return of DST for 2027. This will make sunrise and sunset one hour later.

photo.alt: Clocks being set forward for daylight saving time.

stories.title: Why are judicial races in Michigan separated by incumbency?
stories.summary: Michigan's judicial elections separate incumbent judges into their own ballot sections under a 1982 law lobbied for by sitting judges. This practice allows incumbents to avoid competing directly with challengers, a system critics argue insulates judges from political pressures while proponents claim it protects judicial independence. The law was championed by former state Rep. Virgil C. Smith, who defended it as necessary to shield judges from 'the predatory nature of the political system.'

photo.alt: Why are judicial races in Michigan separated by incumbency?

stories.title: Why does the U.P. have a volcanic ridge?
stories.summary: Michigan's Upper Peninsula, particularly the Keweenaw Peninsula, was shaped by massive volcanic activity over a billion years ago. The Greenstone Flow, part of the Midcontinent Rift System, created the region's ridge and valley topography and contributed to the formation of Lake Superior. This geological history also led to copper deposits that influenced the area's industrial and cultural development.

photo.alt: Greenstone Flow last gasps

stories.title: Why Mike Duggan dropped out of the Michigan governor's race
stories.summary: Independent candidate Mike Duggan has dropped out of the Michigan governor's race with less than six months until midterms. The MichMash episode explores factors behind his decision and reactions from Democrats and Republicans, noting the political climate made an independent victory unlikely despite his potential.

photo.alt: Why Mike Duggan dropped out of the Michigan governor's race

stories.title: Why this Detroit tenants lawsuit is making landlords nervous
stories.summary: A Detroit tenants union is suing the 36th District Court, arguing that landlords should not be allowed to evict tenants or collect rent for properties without a certificate of compliance. Landlords warn this could destabilize Detroit's rental market, potentially leading to foreclosures and higher rents, while tenants hope it will force improvements in housing conditions.

photo.alt: Why this Detroit tenants lawsuit is making landlords nervous

stories.title: Will this be the last time we 'fall back'? Trump pushes end to DST
stories.summary: President Donald Trump is advocating for a permanent end to Daylight Saving Time, but legislation to achieve this faces uncertainty in Congress. The Sunshine Protection Act of 2025 requires Senate approval and Trump's signature, but Senate leadership has questioned its viability. If the bill fails, DST will end on Nov. 1, 2026, at 2 a.m.

photo.alt: Daylight Saving Time clock change illustration

stories.title: Will you still turn clocks back on Nov. 1?
stories.summary: Trump has long supported ending the twice-yearly clock changes, calling the practice 'foolish, inconvenient' and costly. He argues for permanent daylight saving time, citing benefits like fewer traffic accidents and energy savings. The House approved the Sunshine Protection Act in July, but its Senate fate remains uncertain as lawmakers race to act before Nov. 1.

photo.alt: Will you still turn clocks back on Nov. 1?

stories.title: Wisconsin DNR orders Enbridge to halt unpermitted Line 5 bypass work
stories.summary: Wisconsin’s DNR ordered Enbridge to halt unpermitted Line 5 bypass work near Iron County after an Aug. 25 spill. The agency cited a pattern of noncompliance, including unauthorized wetland disturbance, and may pursue enforcement action. Enbridge claims it’s working on cleanup and the bypass simultaneously.

stories.title: Woman fatally stabbed in Downtown Detroit, suspect in custody
stories.summary: A woman in her 30s was fatally stabbed Sunday afternoon in an alley near Woodward Avenue and E. Congress Street in Detroit. The suspect, a man in his 40s, was arrested after a chase. Police are investigating the motive and confirmed there was no prior interaction between the victim and suspect.

stories.summary: Jaquoya Wix, 34, was fatally stabbed in an alley near Woodward Avenue and E Congress Street in Downtown Detroit on Sept. 20 while on her lunch break. Her family confirmed the attack was random, and the suspect has been arrested. Wix was a mother and employee at Chipotle.
